blockers.message: the review record has no `## plan.challenge` section, while roles were active at it
R-privacy-1 (Looked-up e-mail address written to the error log) is high and still open; fix it, or a human accepts the risk or defers it
R-privacy-2 (Chat vendor receives phone, birth date and address it does not need) is high and still open; fix it, or a human accepts the risk or defers it

findings.evidence: throw new NotFoundError(`no customer with e-mail ${email}`);
findings.recommendation: Keep the e-mail address out of the error message, e.g. `throw new NotFoundError("no customer with this e-mail")`. As written, every lookup that matches no customer (a typo, or an address that is not a customer's) reaches `errorHandler` in src/server.ts, which runs `logger.error("request failed", { path: req.path, error: err.message })`, so the typed address lands in the application logs and wherever they are shipped (GDPR Art. 5(1)(c) and 5(1)(f), Art. 32). The 404 body itself stays generic; only the log leaks.
findings.title: Looked-up e-mail address written to the error log

findings.evidence:
user: {
  id: String(customer.id),
  name: customer.name,
  email: customer.email,
  phone: customer.phone,
  birthDate: customer.birth_date,
  address: customer.address,
},
findings.recommendation: The proposal's stated purpose is that the Helply widget "greets the signed-in customer by name, so that the agent knows who they talk to"; the opaque id and the name serve it. Drop `phone`, `birthDate` and `address` (and `email` unless the team states why Helply needs it) from the settings, and select only the columns needed in `customerById`. Today every signed-in customer who opens the chat sends their full record through GET /chat/settings to the browser and on to Helply, a third-party processor (GDPR Art. 5(1)(c) data minimisation, Art. 25, Art. 28).
findings.title: Chat vendor receives phone, birth date and address it does not need

findings.evidence: - [x] personal-data — customers' records are read and the chat vendor receives who is chatting
findings.recommendation: Question for the team: name Helply as a processor in the plan, confirm a data processing agreement (GDPR Art. 28), where it stores the data (Chapter V if outside the EEA), the lawful basis for sharing (Art. 6), and how Helply's copy is retained and erased when a customer is deleted or exercises their rights (Art. 15–17). The code cannot show any of this; only the controller can.
findings.title: Helply as processor: contract, location and lawful basis not identified

findings.evidence: "SELECT id, email, name, phone, birth_date, address FROM customers WHERE lower(email) = lower($1)",
findings.recommendation: The lookup exists so that agents stop asking customers who they are; the route returns the whole record, birth date and address included, to every `support` user. Unless the team states that agents need those fields, return only id, name and e-mail (GDPR Art. 5(1)(c), Art. 25). Recorded with low confidence: what agents actually need is not stated in the plan.
findings.title: Support lookup returns birth date and address to agents by default
